senses.gloss: (b. h.) pr. n. Babel, the city of Babylon; Babylonia, a country of varying limits, chiefly comprising Mesopotamia, a portion of Great Armenia and some neighbouring countries east of the Tigris (v. Neub. Géogr. p. 320). [Owing to the continued political disturbances in Palestine, Babylonia gradually became the centre of Jewish scholarship; hence both the frequent comparisons and jealousies between the East and the West (Babyl. a. Palest.); cmp. אֶרֶץ, חֲנַנְיָה, תַּלְמוּד.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2:33">Y. Snh. I, 19ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 6:8:13">Y. Ned. VI, 40ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>כי מב׳ תצא וכ׳</he> (sarcastic imitation of <cite ref="Isaiah 2:3">Is. II, 3</cite>).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 24a:18">Snh. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>תלמודה של ב׳</he> Babylonian method (Talmud). <he>עולי ב׳</he> those coming from Bab. to visit the Temple, pilgrims.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 5:4">Ned. V, 4</cite> <he>דבר של ע׳ ב׳</he> that in which pilgrims from Bab. (i.e. Jews living abroad) have a share, as the Temple Mount &c. [<cite ref="Makkot 24a">Macc. 24ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>המונה של ב׳</he>, read <cite ref="T00390"><he>רומי</he></cite> as Ms. M.; cmp. <he>אֲרָמִי</he>.]
